title: The Quality of Husband Worth Honoring Across Generations
author: Michael Foster
summary: Foster reproduces Lucy Hutchinson's 17th-century memorial to her husband Colonel John Hutchinson, modernizing the archaic language. Hutchinson's account reveals a man both tough and tender, capable, disciplined, and deeply committed to his wife's person and honor. Her reverence captures a vision of masculine character that integrates strength, gentleness, musical taste, skill, and unwavering fidelity. Foster argues this mutual deep appreciation between spouses should be revived. The piece demonstrates how husbands formed in virtue and wives who honor them create cultural transmission of godly masculinity across generations.
points: Husband integrates toughness with tenderness; capable leader and devoted lover
Marriage demonstrates steady affection that deepens beyond youth and outward beauty
Fatherhood, brotherhood, leadership, and friendship all flow from singular character
Courtship and marriage built on honor, persuasion, and mutual regard for soul
Wives' reverence for husbands is cultural force for transmitting masculine virtue to children
quotes: He was as kind a father, as dear a brother, as good a master, and as faithful a friend as the world had known.
As for his love for his wife, anyone who wished to draw up a rule of honor, kindness, and religion needed only to copy his example.
So steady was his love that when she ceased to be young and lovely, he began to show her the greatest affection.
His love for his wife showed kindness and religion, governing by persuasion and valuing her soul and honor above her beauty.
I would love to see a revival of this kind of deep appreciation between wife and husband, and husband and wife.” Archived from This is Foster on May 2, 2026 by Tim.
